title: The Promise of the Old Mill House Revisited
premise: Marine biologist Felix Oyelaran returns to his late grandmother's crumbling mill house in coastal Maine to settle her estate, still raw from a broken engagement and a career spent hiding behind sea turtle counts. To survive a week-long family reunion orchestrated by his scheming cousin, he recruits Wren Halloway, the vineyard manager next door who inherited her own family's land and its debts, to pose as his partner. The fake date deepens into something real as they restore the mill house together, uncovering letters that reveal Felix's grandmother once chose ambition over love at this very vineyard. When a job offer in Monterey forces Felix to choose between the career that saved him and Wren, he nearly repeats his grandmother's mistake — but arrives back just as the vineyard's first harvest comes in, choosing Wren and turning the mill house into a marine research station rooted in found family.
about_author: Silas Nakamura is a former tide-pool docent who writes love stories set where salt water meets old farmland. He lives in a converted cannery with his partner and an unreasonable number of field notebooks.

chapters.title: Turtles Don't Count Heartbreaks
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. On a research boat in Monterey, Felix counts turtle hatchlings while dodging calls about his grandmother's will. His engagement ended eight months ago; his coping strategy is data. Emotional beat: controlled grief cracking at the edges when the lawyer's letter names the Old Mill House.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Arriving in coastal Maine, Felix learns the will requires him to host the family reunion at the mill house within one month or forfeit it to his cousin Desmond. Emotional beat: resentment curdling into determination as he walks the sagging rooms of his childhood summers.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Vineyard Fence
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren Halloway, managing her late father's debt-ridden vineyard next door, catches Felix measuring the property line and mistakes him for a developer. Their first argument is fierce and oddly electric. Emotional beat: two guarded people recognizing each other's exhaustion.

chapters.title: A Reasonable Proposal
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Desmond announces he's bringing a new fiancée to flaunt at the reunion. Cornered, Felix asks Wren to pose as his partner; she agrees if he helps save her failing first harvest. Emotional beat: a deal struck with too much eye contact.

chapters.title: Rehearsing the Truth
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They invent a meet-cute over cheap wine in the vineyard barn, practicing how they fell in love until the invented details start feeling dangerously plausible. Emotional beat: laughter that neither expected, followed by an awkward, charged silence.

chapters.title: Dust and Photographs
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Cleaning the mill house attic, Felix finds a shoebox of letters between his grandmother and someone signed only 'E.' — dated from the vineyard's founding year. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into unease about what his family never told him.

chapters.title: First Guests, First Cracks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Early relatives arrive; Aunt Bev adores Wren instantly, and Desmond probes their story with lawyerly suspicion. A shared kitchen dance to cover a slip-up feels too real by dessert. Emotional beat: the fake relationship's first involuntary heartbeat.

chapters.title: Saltwater Confessions
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. On a midnight walk to the cove, Felix tells Wren about the engagement that collapsed under his absence, and she admits she gave up a sommelier career in Lyon to save her father's vines. Emotional beat: mutual vulnerability, hands almost touching.

chapters.title: The Letter from E.
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren deciphers the letters: Elias Halloway, her great-grandfather, loved Felix's grandmother, who left him for a marine post abroad. The mill house and vineyard were meant to be joined. Emotional beat: history repeating itself with terrible clarity.

chapters.title: Desmond Moves
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Desmond discovers the will's fine print — proof of a 'stable partnership' is required, and he's hired an investigator. He offers Felix a buyout dressed as mercy. Emotional beat: anger hardening into protectiveness over both houses.

chapters.title: Storm on the Trellis
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A summer storm threatens the harvest; Felix abandons reunion logistics to help stake the vines through the night. Soaked and laughing in the barn afterward, they kiss. Emotional beat: the pretense officially dies, unspoken.

chapters.title: Real by Morning
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Waking tangled together, they agree quietly to be real — but privately, until the reunion ends. Felix drafts a counteroffer to Desmond using the letters as evidence of shared inheritance intent. Emotional beat: fragile, deliberate hope.

chapters.title: The Investigator's Report
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Desmond's investigator photographs them and digs up Wren's debts, presenting the 'relationship' as a scheme to satisfy the will. The family fractures; Aunt Bev defends them, but doubt spreads. Emotional beat: humiliation and the terror of being misread.

chapters.title: Monterey Calls
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix's dream directorship — the job he sacrificed his engagement for — offers a start date during harvest week. His ex even resurfaces, saying he's changed. Emotional beat: the old life glittering exactly when the new one is bleeding.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Chose
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren finds the final letter: Felix's grandmother wrote to Elias the night before leaving, asking him to come, and he never opened it. Wren refuses to be anyone's unopened letter and tells Felix to decide without her. Emotional beat: heartbreak chosen ahead of time, armor up.

chapters.title: The Reunion Dinner
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. At the reunion's climax dinner, Desmond demands a vote on the estate. Felix publicly claims the mill house, reveals the letters, and then — cornered by the investigator's photos — cannot say whether the love is real. Wren leaves the table. Emotional beat: public collapse.

chapters.title: Empty Rows
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren works the vineyard alone at dawn, deciding to sell rather than watch another Halloway wait for someone who chooses elsewhere. Felix is gone; his rental house stands open and hollow. Emotional beat: grief mistaken for certainty.

chapters.title: The Unopened Letter
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Packing in Monterey, Felix rereads his grandmother's last letter and finds a note in her handwriting addressed to him: 'Open your letter, Felix. Timing is a choice, not a fate.' He withdraws from the directorship. Emotional beat: breaking the generational pattern mid-flight.

chapters.title: Driving North Through the Night
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix drives eighteen hours, rehearsing apologies and discarding all of them. He stops only to call Aunt Bev, who tells him the family voted the mill house to him after all — Desmond's investigator was disbarred-adjacent enough to discredit. Emotional beat: fear transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Harvest morning: neighbors, Aunt Bev, and estranged cousins show up to pick grapes alongside Wren. Mid-row, she looks up and sees Felix walking through the vines carrying two coffee cups and his grandmother's letters. Emotional beat: the held breath before forgiveness.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Felix proposes not marriage but a plan: the mill house becomes a small coastal research station, the vineyard supplies its kitchen, and the properties are legally rejoined per the founders' letters. Wren says yes to all of it, then kisses him in front of everyone. Emotional beat: private love made public and permanent.

chapters.title: The Promise of the Old Mill House
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. One year later: first crush bottled, first turtle nest tagged on the cove, reunion now an annual festival. Felix and Wren frame the two founders' letters side by side above the mill house hearth. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined — memory kept alive by choice, not blood.
